Logistic Regression
Logistic Regression
Logistic regression is used in machine learning extensively - every time we need to provide probabilistic semantics to an outcome e.g.\xa0predicting the risk of developing a given disease (e.g.\xa0diabetes; coronary heart disease), based on observed characteristics of the patient (age, sex, body mass index, results of various blood tests, etc.), whether an voter will vote for a given party, predicting the probability of failure of a given process, system or product, predicting a customer’s propensity to purchase a product or halt a subscription, predicting the likelihood of a homeowner defaulting on a mortgage.
Odds and the Logistic Sigmoid
If
\(\sigma\)
is a probability of an event, then the ratio
\(\frac{\sigma}{1-\sigma}\)
is the corresponding
odds
